title: fix(mobile): Enhance transaction execution flow with relaying of Safe-pays transactions
description:
## What it solves Resolves: [PLA-1608](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/PLA-1608/mobile-fix-pay-from-safe-execution-before-gtf-phase-2-rollout) Fixes the **Pay from Safe** (GTF Safe-pays) execution flow on mobile ahead of the GTF Phase 2 rollout, and brings the execute/review fee UI in line with web ## How this PR fixes it **GTF Safe-pays handling (core)** - Safe-pays transactions now take **priority** and are treated as the only valid execution path. The execution method can no longer be switched, the "Execution method" chip reads **"Paid from your Safe"**, is non pressable, and drops the chevron (no "Choose how to execute" sheet, which made no sense for Safe-pays). - The footer shows the full fee breakdown for Safe-pays: **Execution method · Execution fee (FREE) · Max gas fee** (the deterministic max gas fee in the Safe's gas token), instead of the signer's "Est. network fee". Any non-Safe-pays tx behaves exactly as before. - `useExecutionFlow` now maps `SIMULATION_FAILED` to the same explanatory copy as web ("This transaction is expected to fail on-chain, so it can't be relayed. Review the transaction or reject it.") instead of the raw CGW message. **Fee UI** - Added the **Execution fee** row (with info icon → bottom sheet) to the execute footer. - `FeesBreakdown` shows **"Calculated at execution"** and hides "Total outgoing" for signer-pays txs whose gas price isn't fixed yet (mirrors web); Safe-pays still shows the real amounts. - Token-type handling now uses the `isERC20Transfer` guard so ERC-721 transfers no longer fall through; `useTokenDetails` accepts an optional arg (removed an `as never` stub). - The token-transfer header shows the second Safe-paid currency alongside the transfer ("–0.05 ETH · –25 USDC"), with a "Sending" label, matching the 2-currency Figma. - Extracted shared fee copy/components (`feeInfoText`, `FeeLabelWithInfo`) so the footer and the breakdown can't drift. **PR-review findings** - Extracted a single `useRequiresRelay(txDetails)` hook as the source of truth for relay gating, reused in both the picker and the review screen (previously duplicated with divergent UI). Both now render the shared `RelayUnavailableSheet`. - Removed the redundant `useEffect` that dispatched the execution method from the picker — `getExecutionMethod()` already derives it; the highlight is now purely derived. - Extracted a shared `ConfirmationSheet` and rebuilt `IndeterminateSimulationSheet` + `RelayUnavailableSheet` on top of it (they were ~90% identical). ## How to test it 1. Run the mobile app (`yarn workspace @safe-global/mobile start:ios`). 2. **Signer-pays tx (default):** open Review → footer shows "Execution method (signer) · Execution fee FREE · Est. gas fee". A freshly created tx shows "Calculated at execution" with no Total outgoing. 3. **Safe-pays tx (GTF):** open a Pay-from-Safe tx → "Execution method" reads "Paid from your Safe" (non-tappable, no chevron); footer shows "Execution fee FREE · Max gas fee {token amount}". 4. **Indeterminate simulation:** when CGW returns `INDETERMINATE_SIMULATION`, the "Confirm execution" sheet appears with Back / Execute anyway. 5. **Simulation failed:** `SIMULATION_FAILED` routes to the execution-error screen with the web copy. 6. Tap the ⓘ icons on the fee rows → the correct info bottom sheet opens. ## Affected flows - Execute a transaction (signer-pays) — review footer, fee rows, info sheets. - Execute a Pay-from-Safe (GTF) transaction — locked relay method, Safe-token gas fee. - Choose-how-to-execute picker — relay/signer selection, relay-unavailable terminal state. - Indeterminate / failed pre-relay simulation — confirmation sheet and error screen. - Token-transfer confirmation/review header (2-currency Safe-pays display). ## Visual summary ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Review & Execute] --> B{txRequiresRelay?
GTF Safe-pays} B -->|Yes| C[Method: 'Paid from your Safe'
non-tappable, no chevron] C --> D[Execution fee: FREE] D --> E[Max gas fee: amount in Safe gas token] B -->|No| F[Method: signer / 'Sponsored by Safe'
tappable → picker] F --> G[Execution fee: FREE] G --> H[Est. network fee] B -->|Safe-pays but chain has no relay| I[RelayUnavailableSheet
terminal, no signer fallback] ```

findings.claim: The container guards that prevent falling back to the no-signer/double-pay execution route have no tests, even though on chains without relaying the execution-method logic deliberately falls back to WITH_PK, making these guards the only protection against the double-pay path.

determineExecutionPath returns the string 'biometrics' when isBiometricsEnabled is false, which is confusing because it actually signals that the user should be routed to the biometrics opt-in screen; the value should be renamed (e.g. to 'biometrics-opt-in') or the branch inverted.
The useCallback's dependency array includes safe from useSafeInfo(), which has an unstable reference, so it will keep invalidating the memoization of the callback (and the executors table it uses).

IndeterminateSimulationSheet and RelayUnavailableSheet are nearly identical (same BottomSheetModal setup, badge, title, text and button layout) and differ only in icon theme, copy and buttons; a single configurable alert sheet could cover both, similar to how ReadOnlyWarningModal and SoftUpdatePrompt already repeat this pattern.

The new Safe-pays logic has no tests: the effect that forces relay, the terminal RelayUnavailableSheet branch, and the hidden signer list and divider are all untested, and there is no test file for this container at all.

confirmExecuteAnyway has no guard against being triggered twice; unlike handleConfirmPress which checks isExecuting, a double tap on "Execute anyway" before the sheet closes can send two relay requests, both with acceptUnverifiedSimulation: true. A synchronous ref guard shared with runExecution should be added.

This container and ReviewAndExecuteContainer both independently re-derive isRelayEnabled, requiresRelay, and isRelayAvailable, and each renders a different UI for the 'relay not available' terminal state (RelayUnavailableSheet in one, an inline Text in the other), creating duplicated logic and inconsistent UX.

The fee row markup diverges between components: FeesBreakdown.tsx defines and uses FeeRow/FeeAmount components, while ReviewExecuteFooter.tsx re-implements the fee rows inline with raw View flexDirection="row" and TokenAmount, resulting in subtly different styling (e.g. the footer uses fontWeight={700} while the breakdown uses $success text only) for what should be the same 'Execution fee · FREE' and 'Max gas fee' rows; FeeRow/FeeAmount should be exported and shared alongside FeeLabelWithInfo so the visual contract is consistent.
The tooltip text was copied from the web app's tooltip source and has already drifted out of sync, missing the trailing phrase "...on the blockchain."
SIMULATION_CODES manually copies a generated union type rather than referencing it directly, risking drift if the generated type changes.

The condition BigInt(outgoing.amount) > 0n drops the outgoing line entirely when the amount is zero, which is correct for value transfers but incorrect for zero-value calls that should still display the destination, such as NFT mints or contract calls shown as transfers.

The execute button area shows "Free" for Safe-pays transactions even though the Safe actually pays the relayer back through handlePayment, so the correct "Paid from your Safe" wording only appears inside an info tooltip rather than in the primary fee display.
simulationError and retryWithAcceptUnverified appear to be dead code since nothing reads them and useExecutionFlow already owns this flow.
The new safePaidFee branch, which decides whether to show "amount · fee" when the gas token differs from the transfer token, has no test; the existing test only covers the pure builder function.

transferTokenAddress reads transferInfo.tokenAddress from an untyped Record<string, unknown>, losing the Erc20/Erc721/NativeCoin type distinction that TokenTransfer.tsx already obtains via the isERC20Transfer type guard, which could let ERC-721 transfers fall through incorrectly.

The tests only exercise the WITH_RELAY branch of the four-branch dispatcher refactor (executors object at lines 53-97 of useTransactionExecution.ts), so a regression in executors[executionMethod] selecting PK/Ledger/WC would not be caught.
The executors dispatch table is reallocated on every render even though it is only used inside the useCallback defined at lines 99-144; it should be moved inside the callback or wrapped in useMemo.
The UI string "FREE" is rendered in all caps, which is the only all-caps label in the sheet and is inconsistent with the project's sentence-case convention for labels.

These two folders are missing the index.ts barrel file that all seven sibling folders have, so their imports go directly to the file instead of through a barrel, inconsistent with documented code style.

The fee-breakdown computation is duplicated in both TokenTransfer.tsx and FeesBreakdown.tsx for the same transaction, and should be cached via a single shared hook (e.g. useFeesBreakdown(executionInfo, txInfo)) so the two computations cannot drift apart.

The max gas fee is displayed even when the fee is not paid from the Safe; for an ordinary transaction this computes to 0, so co-signers see wording like "Execution fee FREE / Max gas fee 0 MATIC / Paid from the signer" instead of an accurate state, whereas web hides this behind a feature check and shows "Calculated at execution".
There is no component test covering the null-return case of the fees breakdown component or the "Paid from your Safe / signer" wording.

useTokenDetails(transfer ?? ({ transferInfo: {} } as never)) passes a fake object with an as never cast to bypass the type system, which has the same risk as using any; the hook should instead accept an optional argument or support being skipped.

The rule that sums fee rows for the same token into one line re-implements logic that already exists in web's totalOutgoing service, duplicating logic that should live in the shared packages directory per project conventions.

This container duplicates the relay-availability derivation logic and renders a different 'relay not available' UI than HowToExecuteSheet.container.tsx, compounding the duplication described for that file.
The name FeesBreakdown is used both for a function and elsewhere, creating a naming collision; it may be clearer to rename this to FeesBreakdownData.
The simulation error is not displayed anywhere to the user, and it is unclear whether this is intentional; it is also unclear what happens if the CGW is unable to relay the transaction.

IndeterminateSimulationSheet and RelayUnavailableSheet share nearly identical BottomSheetModal scaffolding, badge, title, body, and button layout, with subtle inconsistencies in icon names, paddings, and badge themes, indicating they should share a common ConfirmationSheet component to prevent drift.

An effect dispatches setExecutionMethod(WITH_RELAY) when requiresRelay && isRelayEnabled, but getExecutionMethod() in helpers.ts already enforces this at compute-time, so the effect causes an unnecessary extra render and redundant write to the Redux slice.

Two different ways to find the transfer token address were added in the same change: FeesBreakdown uses a loosely typed transferTokenAddress helper taking a Record<string, unknown>, while TokenTransfer.tsx uses the existing isERC20Transfer guard; both should use isERC20Transfer, and both files also duplicate the same native-currency object construction ({ address: ZERO_ADDRESS, symbol, decimals }).

The fee breakdown component is rendered on every pending transaction without checking whether the GTF feature is enabled, so it can show fee information on chains or configurations where it shouldn't appear at all.

Relay is now forced for Safe-pays transactions, but the UI text still says "Sponsored by Safe · We pay transactions fees for you · {remaining} left / day", and the remaining count can incorrectly show "0 left / day" because the daily limit is skipped for these transactions.

txRequiresRelay is imported from another feature's internals (features/ExecuteTx/components/ReviewAndExecute/helpers) even though it is a pure check with no component dependency; it could move to packages/utils alongside isGtfSafePaid or into a shared util.

The terminal state rendered when requiresRelay && !isRelayEnabled is untested; existing tests cover the pure helper functions txRequiresRelay and getExecutionMethod but not this rendering branch, and neither new sheet component has a test.
Number(formatUnits(...)) loses precision for amounts with 18 decimals; this is acceptable for fiat display but should have a comment noting the tradeoff.

retryWithAcceptUnverified calls execute(true) without awaiting or catching it, and since execute re-throws, any failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection; the existing retry function has the same problem and this change copies it.

Three callers of buildFeesBreakdown (FeesBreakdown.tsx, ReviewExecuteFooter.tsx, and TokenTransfer.tsx) each independently read selectActiveChainCurrency from the store and build the same native-currency object with address, symbol, and decimals, duplicating logic and the if (!nativeCurrency) return undefined guard across call sites; this repetition should be extracted into a shared hook such as useFeesBreakdown that owns the store reads and native-currency mapping.

Number(fiatConversion) converts an empty or whitespace-only string to 0, which passes the Number.isFinite check, so a price that is actually unknown would display as $0 instead of being omitted; an empty or trimmed-empty string should be treated as undefined.

The new return fields simulationError and retryWithAcceptUnverified are only used in the hook's own test file, while the real flow goes through useExecutionFlow.confirmExecuteAnyway instead, leaving two parallel retry APIs; they should either be removed or wired up.

The label "FREE" is rendered in all caps instead of sentence case; additionally, fees are now always shown on the confirm screen, a "Sending" label was added to the transfer header, and signer execution was removed for Safe-pays transactions, and these visible product changes should link to the product or design decision in the PR description.

fontSize={16} lineHeight={24} are hardcoded numeric values rather than Tamagui design tokens (e.g. fontSize="$4"), which the project's structure guidelines call for, though this raw-number pattern already exists elsewhere in the codebase.

useTokenDetails is called with a stub value cast away with 'as never' (transfer ?? ({ transferInfo: {} } as never)), which hides a type mismatch; the hook's parameter should be made explicitly optional or the values should be lifted out conditionally before calling it.
There is no test coverage for the new txRequiresRelay function or for the requiresRelay = true branch of getExecutionMethod, even though these gate the no-fallback execution flow.
The same bottom-sheet boilerplate is duplicated a third time across two components instead of reusing the existing implementation from SoftUpdatePrompt.tsx.
The new safe-paid fee header amount has no tests.
The relay execution flow now fails whenever getSafeSDK() is not set, matching a guard already present in the WalletConnect executor, but worth confirming is intentional and consistent.
